item.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85

description.p: Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile

Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.

Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

item.title: ‘I’m genuinely sorry’: Australian Hyrox athlete who soiled herself apologises to China and rivals

li.p: Joanna Wietrzyk ‘regrets’ decision to keep racing
She forfeits points from her win in the Beijing race

description.p: The Australian athlete who caused a storm by winning a Hyrox event in China despite soiling herself during the race has apologised to the “people of China” and rival athletes in a statement online.

Posting on Instagram, Joanna Wietrzyk offered a “sincere apology” to the “people of China, my fellow competitors, the spectators and the Hyrox organizers for what happened during the race in Beijing”.

item.title: Thursday briefing: Yemen’s war continues to threaten oil supplies– but what about its people?

description.p: In today’s newsletter: The Houthi advance along the Red Sea coast raised fears for global trade and energy supplies, while more than 100,000 Yemenis have been displaced by the fighting
Good morning. The lightning advance of Houthi militants along the west coast of Yemen over the past week has prompted fears of a spiralling conflict in the region and a new oil supply crisis.

For families living in the Middle East’s poorest country, the most significant fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces in years is a crisis upon a catastrophe, with escalating civilian casualties and at least 100,000 displaced in recent days.

item.title: UN spokesperson warns humanitarian situation in Yemen is deteriorating

a.span: UN spokesperson warns humanitarian situation in Yemen is deteriorating

div.p: UN Secretary-General spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned on Thursday that the humanitarian situation in Yemen is worsening as tensions escalate in the region.

UN Human Rights Office verified 55 civilian casualties from 19 incidents in the governorates of Taiz, Hodeidah, Marib and Lahj since the start of the month, adding that the actual toll was likely to be much higher, Dujarric said.

Among them, 16 people were killed, including 10 children, he added, while restrictions to access, funding shortages and security incidents involving humanitarian premises were hindering the international response.

item.title: US says it will sell up to 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia

a.span: US says it will sell up to 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia

footer.div: Submitted by Sean Mathews on Thu, 09/17/2026 - 19:44

div.div: The Trump administration has been working on the sale for months, but the key announcement comes as the kingdom battles Yemen's Houthis
An Israeli F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft does a flyover during an air show in Tel Aviv, on 26 April 2023 (Jack Guez/AFP)

div.p: The US State Department has notified Congress that it plans to sell Saudi Arabia up to 48 F-35 warplanes, in a move that has been widely opposed by Israel.
The historic sale could total $24.3bn and would mark the first time an Arab state gains access to the US’s fifth-generation jet fighter.

“This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a major non-NATO ally that is a force for political stability and economic progress in the Gulf region,” the State Department said in a statement on Thursday.
Middle East Eye has reported on the progress of the sale for months, with multiple US and Arab sources saying it was moving quickly.

MEE revealed in November that Saudi Arabia’s F-35 purchase would be “fast-tracked” under a new defence partnership with the US, sealed during Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s visit to the White House.

MEE then revealed in December that the Trump administration was conducting a review of Israel's qualitative military edge (QME) as part of the process. Senior US military officials held several closely guarded meetings on Capitol Hill to discuss the sale at the start of the year.
Saudi Arabian Defence Minister Khaled bin Salman visited the US multiple times this summer, in part to ensure the deal went through, US officials told MEE.
While the sale has been in the works for months, the State Department’s public announcement comes at a critical time for the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia is reeling from Houthi missile and drone attacks while its allies in Yemen, the internationally recognised government, are struggling to stem a Houthi offensive that has resulted in them securing the entirety of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline, along with the Arabian Gulf side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
The announcement is a defeat for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who campaigned against selling F-35s to Saudi Arabia.
The concept of an Israeli QME over Arab militaries goes back to the Cold War.

div.div: Trump administration reviewing Israel's 'military edge' as it eyes Gulf arms deals, sources say

div.p: In 1979, the US brokered a peace treaty between Israel and Egypt, then the Arab world's dominant military power alongside Iran. Egypt's peace with Israel was underwritten by the promise of US military aid, which Israel wanted to ensure was inferior to the weapons it received.

In 2008, Congress codified Israel's QME into a law that also mandated periodic assessments of US arms sales to Arab states. The F-35 can be downgraded or upgraded based on packages like radar and stealth features, similar to how buyers can choose different trim levels of a car.

p.span: Israel has unparalleled access to the F-35 and even modified the warplane with additional fuel capacity to conduct long-range attacks on Iran without the need for refuelling, MEE revealed.

div.p: US officials told MEE that Saudi Arabia would purchase F-35s without all the enhancements Israel has, but what modifications it will entail is likely to be extremely guarded.
The sale has irked some members of the US defence and intelligence community who believe China will gain access to critical US technologies if Saudi Arabia operates the warplane.
One day before the State Department’s announcement, The New York Times published a story citing US officials raising those concerns.

item.title: At least 63 killed in latest fighting between Yemen government, Houthis

a.span: At least 63 killed in latest fighting between Yemen government, Houthis

div.p: Fighting between the Houthis and Yemeni government forces and their Saudi backers has killed 63 people in the last 24 hours, AFP reported on Thursday, citing military sources from both sides.

At least 23 government soldiers were killed in missile and drone attacks by the Houthis in two southwestern provinces, a government official said, while Houthi military sources reported 40 fighters killed in Saudi air strikes and fighting on the ground.

item.title: Fighting in Yemen pushing health system to ‘collapse’, says WHO chief

a.span: Fighting in Yemen pushing health system to ‘collapse’, says WHO chief

div.p: Escalating tensions in Yemen are “pushing an already fragile health system closer to collapse”, director general of the World Health Organisation Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned on Thursday.

“Nearly 20 million people need health assistance, while outbreaks of cholera, measles, polio and dengue, as well as malnutrition, threaten more lives,” Ghebreyesus wrote on X, adding “peace is the best medicine”.
